name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item scale (GAD-7)
instructions: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?

items.text: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen

functionalItem.text: If you checked off any problems, how difficult have these problems made it for you to do your work, take care of things at home, or get along with other people?

bands.label: Minimal anxiety
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the minimal range. A low total does not rule out an anxiety-related concern, so consider it alongside the interview and history; clinical judgment decides.

bands.label: Mild anxiety
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the mild range. Consider watchful monitoring and repeating the scale over time to see the trend; clinical judgment decides.

bands.label: Moderate anxiety
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the moderate range. A total of 10 or more is the commonly cited cutoff that calls for further evaluation, so consider a fuller assessment of anxiety and related conditions; clinical judgment decides.

bands.label: Severe anxiety
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the severe range, above the cutoff of 10 for further evaluation. Consider a prompt, thorough assessment and a discussion of care options with the client; clinical judgment decides.

citation: Spitzer RL, Kroenke K, Williams JBW, Löwe B. A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: the GAD-7. Arch Intern Med. 2006;166(10):1092-1097.
